alternate_titles: The Gospel of St. Mark in Tangkhul Naga (1909)
publisher: British and Foreign Bible Society, Calcutta / Baptist Mission Press
subject: Biblical Literature & Vernacular Translation
notes: 1909 publication of St. Mark in Tangkhul Naga by Rev. William Pettigrew. Presents dynamic narrative prose, action-oriented discourse particles, and early linguistic orthography. Public Domain.

front_matter.title_page: Pa o Kamata Isha mai Jesu Christawui Khararchan: Mark Kahona Kasa (1909)
front_matter.preface: The Gospel of Mark is characterized by rapidity of action and direct vivid narration. Translated by William Pettigrew and published by BFBS in 1909. In Tangkhul, frequent narrative connectives like 'chitharan' (thereupon) and 'khamathān' (immediately) showcase vernacular verbal sequencing.

chapters.title: The Ministry of John the Baptist & Baptism of Jesus (Mark 1)
chapters.summary: The voice crying in the wilderness and the opening of the gospel narrative in Tangkhul.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Mark 1:1-4: Jesu Christa, Varivarawui Naomayārwui khararchan kaphung: Isaiah kaho tui-theikhanana kasa thada leiri: 'Theilu, Nawui mik-ngalemli Iwui pao-phungnaoli kasho vaye, ana nawui shongfa ngalunghang sara. Ramkashilashili khongyui akhana hohe: 'Prohowui shongfa kapanglu, Awui lambili mashunglu.' Johnna ramkashilashili baptism kasami thotna, kala yorshi ngashankahavai ningkaphuritwui baptism pao phongie.
chapters.english_translation: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee. The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.
exercises: Identify the prophetic title given to John the Baptist.

chapters.title: The Stilling of the Storm (Mark 4)
chapters.summary: Miracle on the Sea of Galilee demonstrating authority over wind and waves in Tangkhul description.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Mark 4:35-41: Chi zingsho ngazing-tharan, Ana athumli hang: 'Ngashakazil kakahara kachili ithum ngakorva-u.' Kala mikumo kachungli kashikahailaga, A kuphungli leisai thada thukpingserie. Chitharan hu-hu kaho huimayon kasham akhata rarer, kala tui-ngachaona kuphung tharili ngashingye, chithada kuphung chi tui eina kashung thotna. Kala A kuphung wui kashikli mikazak akhali luipatlaga ngaphamsai: kala athumna ali pholaga hang: 'Tuitamkasana, ithum mathira chi Nawui ningli malei-macho?' Kala A shoklaga huili kaphangserie, kala ngashakazilli hang: 'Maza-lu, ngacham-lu!' Chitharan huichi ngachaoran thotna, kala chitharan ngakazil khamatha akhata shokserie.
chapters.english_translation: And the same day, when the even was come, he saith unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side. And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
grammar_notes: Two-part imperative command: 'Maza-lu, ngacham-lu!' (Be silent, be peaceful!).
Ingressive aspectual particle: 'thotna' denoting rapid onset of state.
exercises: Contrast the terms for boat/canoe ('kuphung') and sea/lake ('ngashakazil').
Identify the verb for rebuking the elements ('kaphang').

chapters.title: The Feeding of the Five Thousand (Mark 6)
chapters.summary: Multiplication of the five loaves and two fishes in Tangkhul hospitality idiom.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Mark 6:38-44: Ana athumli hang: 'Nathumli raruikatha kaphara lei? Vayanglu.' Kala theilaga athumna hang: 'Phangā lei, kala ngachayei khani lei.' Ana athumpup-li haikaphā salaga kacham eina ngashalungli pamkazip milu hoda hangserie. Kala athum thakharā eina, phangā-magā eina ngaburlaga pamserie. Kala Ana raruikatha phangā chi kala ngachayei khani chi khuilaga, kazingli yanglaga Varivarali mathat-eina kashaklaga raruikatha chi khakserie; kala mikumo tharili shunsangserie. Kala athumpup shaksarlaga phasa kashung thotna.
chapters.english_translation: He saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes. And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass. And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties. And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them. And they did all eat, and were filled.
grammar_notes: Distributive numerical expressions: 'thakharā eina, phangā-magā eina' (by hundreds, by fifties).
Completive satiety marker: 'phasa kashung thotna' (their bodies became completely satisfied).
exercises: How does Tangkhul express communal grouping during feasts?
What verb root describes blessing and breaking bread?

chapters.title: The Greatest Commandment & The Widow's Mite (Mark 12)
chapters.summary: Love for God and neighbor, alongside the sacrificial offering of the poor widow.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Mark 12:29-31, 42-44: Jesuna ngahanmi: 'Hingchithei kaphāmeina hi: O Israel, kapeilu; Proho ithui Varivara, Proho akhachana! Kala nawui lungkashung eina, nawui mangazing eina, nawui ning-kacham eina Proho nawui Varivarali ngayeilu: hi hingchithei khare. Kala khakhane chi hithada: 'Nawui aphasa thada nawui ngalemwui mikumoli ngayeilu.' ...Kala ngalashang kacham akha rarlaga paisa khani haksangie. Jesuna hang: 'Ngalashang hi ana kachikathāna haksangmeiserie; kasakei a kacham thotli awui ringkaphavai leikashap kuppup haksangserie.'
chapters.english_translation: And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. ...And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites. And Jesus said, This poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.
grammar_notes: Instrumental postposition 'eina' emphasizing holistic totality ('with all thy heart').
Comparative superiority: 'haksangmeiserie' (cast in far more than all).
exercises: Translate the summary of the Law into colloquial Tangkhul.
Explain the ethical significance of the widow's sacrificial giving.

chapters.title: The Resurrection & Final Commission (Mark 16)
chapters.summary: The empty tomb at sunrise and the mandate to proclaim good tidings everywhere.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Mark 16:1-6: Sabbath ngaphalaga, Mary Magdalene, Jameswui ava Mary, kala Salomena rarlaga Awui phasa kakhalaphavai meithei-chot khuisangserie. Kala hoptawui zingsho khareli, zingkhamathān shoklakha lungkhorli rarlakna. Kala theilu, lungphung kashang chi lunkhor khong eina khangayot theiserie. Kala lungkhor tharili zanglaga kashang-phā chon kachak kazang mayarnaowon akha pamsai theilaga athum ngachek-kashung thotna. Kha ana athumli hang: 'Mangachek-alu: Nazarethwui Jesu, thingkhamirangli kahom chi nathum khayore; A ngatekrarlaga thotsangie; A hili maleira: theilu, A pili kahai pam hi!'
chapters.english_translation: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him. And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun. And they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great. And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were affrighted. And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.

vocabulary.meaning: having risen triumphantly, awakened from death

exercises: Trace the narrative arc from grief to proclamation in Mark 16.

chapters.title: Lexical Concordance of the Gospel of Mark
chapters.summary: Specialized vocabulary of action verbs, directional postpositions, and miracle terms in Mark.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Tuiwon Kasakakhui:
1. Huimayon -- Tempestuous wind storm
2. Kuphung -- Sea boat / fishing canoe
3. Maza-lu -- Peace / silence (imperative)
4. Lungkhor -- Stone tomb / burial cavern
5. Thingkhamirang -- The Cross
6. Ngatekrarlaga -- Risen from the dead
7. Ningkaphurit -- Repentance of heart
8. Ramkashilashi -- Wilderness tract
chapters.english_translation: Action vocabulary and geographical terminology compiled from the 1909 translation of Mark.
exercises: Write five sentences using the vocabulary of Mark 4.

pages.title: The Resurrection & Final Commission (Mark 16)
lines: Summary: The empty tomb at sunrise and the mandate to proclaim good tidings everywhere....
Mark 16:1-6: Sabbath ngaphalaga, Mary Magdalene, Jameswui ava Mary, kala
Salomena rarlaga Awui phasa kakhalaphavai meithei-chot khuisangserie.
Kala hoptawui zingsho khareli, zingkhamathān shoklakha lungkhorli
rarlakna. Kala theilu, lungphung kashang chi lunkhor khong eina
khangayot theiserie. Kala lungkhor tharili zanglaga kashang-phā chon
kachak kazang mayarnaowon akha pamsai theilaga athum ngachek-kashung
thotna. Kha ana athumli hang: 'Mangachek-alu: Nazarethwui Jesu,
thingkhamirangli kahom chi nathum khayore; A ngatekrarlaga thotsangie; A
hili maleira: theilu, A pili kahai pam hi!'
And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of
James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and
anoint him. And very early in the morning the first day of the week,
they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun. And they saw that
the stone was rolled away: for it was very great. And entering into the
sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a
long white garment; and they were affrighted. And he saith unto them, Be
not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is
risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.

pages.tangkhul_content:

1. Huimayon -- Tempestuous wind storm
2. Kuphung -- Sea boat / fishing canoe
3. Maza-lu -- Peace / silence (imperative)
4. Lungkhor -- Stone tomb / burial cavern
5. Thingkhamirang -- The Cross
6. Ngatekrarlaga -- Risen from the dead
7. Ningkaphurit -- Repentance of heart
8. Ramkashilashi -- Wilderness tract
